subject: business-studies

moments.title: The Practice of Management
moments.body: Drucker publishes 'The Practice of Management', arguing that management is a distinct professional discipline and that the firm's purpose is to create a customer. He introduces 'management by objectives' as a framework.

quote.text: There is only one valid definition of business purpose: to create a customer.

moments.takeaway: Management before Drucker was a craft passed on within firms. After, it became a teachable discipline with its own literature.

moments.title: Knowledge worker named
moments.body: Drucker coins 'knowledge worker' to describe the post-industrial labour force. The implication: productivity in knowledge work needs different tools from physical work.
moments.takeaway: By the 2020s, knowledge work makes up the majority of employment in advanced economies — a transition Drucker named decades early.

now.title: Drucker's legacy
now.body: Drucker's MBO is now taught alongside more recent variants (OKRs, used at Intel from Andy Grove in the 1970s and at Google from 1999). The shift from manufacturing to knowledge work continues to drive changes in how firms are managed.
now.open_questions: How do you measure productivity in knowledge work? It's still an unresolved problem, sharpened by remote work post-2020.

reflection: Drucker wrote 39 books across 65 years. The breadth — economics, sociology, ethics, management practice — is hard to imitate now that academic disciplines are more siloed.
